item.title: Dhruv Rathee released hours after detention ahead of CJP protest
item.description:
YouTuber Dhruv Rathee, who was detained by Delhi Police ahead of the Cockroach Janta Party’s (CJP) planned protest at Jantar Mantar on Saturday, was released late at night, a police officer said, NDTV reported.
Rathee was detained at his residence in Gurugram’s Sector 56 as police stepped up security across the national capital to prevent protesters from reaching Jantar Mantar. The demonstration called for Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar’s resignation over alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.
“He can be detained again, or further legal action might be taken if he tries to go to Jantar Mantar despite prohibitory orders,” a police officer told PTI.
In a post on X, the CJP, a political satirical group, alleged that around 50 plainclothes police personnel arrived at Rathee’s home at 8am on Saturday and detained him.
Rathee is a supporter of Congress MP Rahul Gandhi and a vocal critic of the BJP-led National Democratic Alliance (NDA) government.
CJP members Abhijeet Dipke, Sourav Das and Ashutosh Ranka were also placed under preventive detention on Saturday morning before being released by an executive magistrate.
More than 3,000 protesters, including politicians, were detained on Saturday and released later that night, according to the report.
Police established an extensive security cordon around the national capital to prevent unrest near Jantar Mantar in central Delhi. The restrictions also led protesters to split into smaller gatherings across the city.
Meanwhile, the Supreme Court was expected to hold a special sitting on Sunday to hear a contempt petition over the blanket closure of Delhi Metro stations and the suspension of train services on Saturday.
Metro services resumed on Sunday morning, although security remained tight at station entrances and exits. Buses were also stationed nearby to transport people detained by police.
On Friday, a bench comprising Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana had directed that metro services should not be completely suspended ahead of Saturday’s planned protest.

item.title: Child marriage must be eradicated
item.description:
As we observe the International Day of the Girl Child under the vital theme: “End Child Marriage and Invest in Girls’ Rights,” our own country must contend with a harsh reality that we simply cannot ignore.
As per numerous international organizations, nearly half the girls in Bangladesh are married before the age of 18. Despite decades of advocacy and impressive gains in girls' school enrollment and education, that our society loses half of its girls to the pervasive, ruinous scourge of child marriage is nothing if not tragic.
When millions of young girls are pulled out of classrooms, it is a direct assault on human rights, bodily autonomy, and the future potential of our nation.
Child marriage has long been a devastating barrier for Bangladesh’s development. Not only does it prematurely end education and expose young girls to severe health risks, it simultaneously perpetuates intergenerational cycles of poverty and strips them of their fundamental agency.
We have long had laws on paper, yet enforcement has been all but missing. Local loopholes, social pressure, and the failure of community-level administrative tracking has allowed child marriages to occur with alarming frequency, particularly in our rural and marginalized communities.
Investing in girls' rights requires moving past passive declarations and demands an unyielding, zero-tolerance approach that not only prosecutes those who perpetuate this archaic practise, but also informs and educates the people about the dangers of it.
A nation cannot rise when half its population is forced into premature servitude. Protecting our daughters, keeping them in school, and guaranteeing their right to choose their own destiny is a non-negotiable prerequisite for the kind of Bangladesh we want to be in.
The eradication of child marriage has been an urgent national emergency for far too long, and it is time we start taking concrete actions to address it.

item.title: Turning waste to opportunity
item.description:
Prime Minister Tarique Rahman’s assurance of state support for a potentially groundbreaking waste-to-fuel technology could be the glimmer of hope needed for Bangladesh’s energy future.
Developed over a decade of rigorous laboratory research by scientists at Khulna University of Engineering and Technology (KUET), the process presents an elegant solution to two of our most pressing national crises: Urban waste accumulation and heavy reliance on imported fossil fuels.
If successfully scaled, converting sewage, agricultural residue, and kitchen waste into high-grade biocrude could save the country thousands of crore annually in foreign exchange while tackling severe environmental pollution.
However, even beyond the potential for such a process, we must encourage more of such home-grown innovation that represents the exact kind of forward-thinking science that our country urgently needs.
For decades, our city corporations have struggled under the weight of unmanaged waste while the energy sector remains perpetually vulnerable to volatile global fuel markets and foreign currency shortages. A technology that addresses sanitation while producing domestic fuel is a significant win-win that deserves backing from the highest levels of government.
However, high-level verbal assurances alone do not build infrastructure, as we continue to unfortunately witness. Our history is littered with promising pilot concepts and academic breakthroughs that withered away in bureaucratic limbo due to a lack of timely funding, institutional coordination, and commercial scaling.
To that end, we are hopeful about the pilot project processing one to three tons of waste daily to assess the technology’s efficiency, production costs, and commercial viability. The estimated cost of the pilot project is Tk100-120 crore, and we hope that the government firmly supports its implementation to ensure its success.
If we are truly committed to sustainable energy security and green innovation, we must encourage more innovation. At present, we have a potentially game-changing homegrown solution - we must ensure it is given the capital, urgency, and institutional priority required.

item.title: Dhaka ranks 6th most polluted city
item.description:
Dhaka ranked 6th among the world's most polluted cities on Sunday morning, recording an Air Quality Index (AQI) score of 166 at 8:31am.
The air quality was classified as "unhealthy", meaning the concentration of pollutants in the air has reached a level that could pose health risks to the general population, according to the AQI scale.
Kolkata in India ranked first with an AQI score of 187, while Singapore ranked second with a score of 184, followed by Hanoi in Vietnam in the third place with an AQI score of 178.
According to AQI standards, a reading between 101 and 150 is considered "unhealthy for sensitive groups", while 151 to 200 is classified as "unhealthy". A reading between 201 and 300 is considered "very unhealthy", while levels above 301 are deemed "hazardous", posing serious health risks.
The AQI provides daily updates on air quality, indicating how clean or polluted the air is and highlighting potential health impacts.
In Bangladesh, the AQI is calculated based on five major pollutants: particulate matter (PM10 and PM2.5), nitrogen dioxide (NO2), carbon monoxide (CO), sulfur dioxide (SO2) and ozone.
Dhaka has long struggled with air pollution, with air quality typically deteriorating during winter and improving during the monsoon season.
The World Health Organization estimates that air pollution causes around seven million deaths globally each year, mainly from stroke, heart disease, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, lung cancer and acute respiratory infections.

item.title: Spain beat US 2-0 in clash between world’s top-ranked women’s teams
item.description:
Spain scored twice in the opening 14 minutes before goalkeeper Adriana Nanclares saved a second-half penalty to beat the United States 2-0 on Saturday in a showdown between the world’s top two women’s football teams.
Patri Guijarro opened the scoring with a long-range strike in the third minute, beating US goalkeeper Claudia Dickey. Eva Navarro then volleyed home Salma Paralluelo’s cross to extend Spain’s lead.
The match was the first of two friendly matches between reigning Women’s World Cup champions Spain and Olympic champions the United States. The teams, who have won the last three World Cups between them, will meet again Tuesday near Philadelphia.
US coach Emma Hayes said her side could not afford to give Spain an early advantage, while defender Emily Fox praised the opponents’ clinical finishing.
The Americans created several chances, but Nanclares denied Sophia Wilson and later saved Lily Yohannes’ penalty. Wilson also had a goal ruled out for offside following a video review.
Spain were reduced to 10 players late in the match after Athenea del Castillo received a red card for apparently pulling an American player’s hair.
Several key players missed the contest, including Spain’s three-time Ballon d’Or winner Aitana Bonmatí and US defenders Naomi Girma and Emily Sonnett.
Mallory Swanson returned for the US in the 66th minute, making her first national-team appearance in more than 700 days after parental leave.

item.title: Messi nets brace to win in first match after Argentina exit
item.description:
Lionel Messi scored twice to help Inter Miami rout DC United 4-0 on Saturday, taking a victory in his first match since saying farewell to the Argentina national team.
Four nights after scoring in his final match for the Albiceleste in a victory over Benin, the 39-year-old South American superstar struck in the 47th and 60th minutes as defending MLS champion Miami won for only the second time in their past 11 league matches.
A first-half brace by Luis Suarez staked the Herons to the lead as they improved to 13-5 with 10 drawn for 49 points, jumping from third to second in the Eastern Conference
Messi hopes to make Miami the first team to win back-to-back MLS crowns since the Los Angeles Galaxy in 2011-12.
Messi, the top point producer in the league with 23 goals plus assists on 13 others, seeks a third consecutive MLS Most Valuable Player award.
Uruguayan striker Suarez scored in the third minute to give Miami the lead, blasting a left-footed shot from the heart of the box into the top left corner.
Suarez struck again in the 39th for his 16th goal of the campaign, assisted like his first of the night by German Berterame.
Messi blasted home a left-footed shot off an assist from Suarez to give Miami a 3-0 lead and evaded three defenders to add another goal 13 minutes later as the pink-clad hosts pulled away to stay.
In other games, Scottish striker Lewis Morgan and American Djordje Mihailovic scored in second-half stoppage time to rally Toronto for a 2-1 home victory over Montreal.
The visitors grabbed the lead in the Canadian clash on a goal by Mexican forward Daniel Rios in the 52nd minute.
Toronto, however, battled back for the equalizer by winger Morgan, obtained last month from San Diego, in the third minute of stoppage time, his first regular-season MLS goal in two years.
Former Montreal standout Mihailovic struck for the decider in the fifth minute of extra time.
"Now I've scored on both sides of this derby," he said. "It feels good."
Toronto snapped a three-game losing streak to pull within a point of an East playoff berth.
At Chicago, Swiss forward Maren Haile-Selassie scored in the 87th minute to give the 10-man Chicago Fire a 2-1 triumph over New York City.
Austrian midfielder Hannes Wolf gave City the lead in the 19th minute and Chicago dropped to 10 men when Ivory coast midfielder Dje D'Avilla received his second yellow card in the 43rd minute.
Swede Anton Saletros equalized for Chicago in the 55th minute, setting the stage for the decider.

item.title: Barca extend perfect streak, Real survive Vinicius red
item.description:
Anthony Gordon scored his first goal for Barcelona as the Spanish champions extended their perfect start in La Liga with a 3-0 win over Getafe on Saturday.
Real Madrid finished with 10 men against Villarreal after Vinicius Junior was sent off for hair pulling in a 1-0 victory, with Yan Diomande's goal keeping Jose Mourinho's side, third, on Barcelona's trail.
Los Blancos are six points behind Barca, who also lead second-place Atletico Madrid by five points after Diego Simeone's team snatched a late 2-1 win at Alaves.
England winger Gordon opened the scoring for Barca in the second minute and Gabriel Jesus added another after half an hour for the league leaders, who have won every match they have played this season.
France defender Jules Kounde tucked home the third from Lamine Yamal's cross to cap Barca's solid win against Jose Bordalas's side at Camp Nou.
Barca were without their top scorer Raphinha, who sustained a hamstring problem during the international break with Brazil.
Flick replaced him with former Arsenal striker and Selecao compatriot Jesus and his side came roaring out of the blocks.
"Being at Barca is a dream... playing with these players is very easy too, everyone plays very well," Jesus told DAZN after his first start and third goal for the club.
"That makes it easier for me as a striker, to have chances, and I'm ready to score the goals...
"(But) I hope Rafa can recover quickly, because of course the team misses him."
Gordon, who has impressed since joining this summer, grabbed his first Barca goal with a low deflected effort after bundling his way past three players.
He was Barca's brightest spark in the first half, continuing his fine goalscoring form for England in the recent Nations League matches.
"He's doing very well," said Flick of Gordon. "He scored with England. He has a lot of confidence... he gives us a lot."
Getafe defender Zaid Romero gave the ball away in his own box for Barca's second, passing it straight to Jesus, who stroked into the bottom corner.
The otherwise quiet Yamal supplied Kounde for the third as Barca secured a ninth win from nine games across all competitions.
Diomande, Real Madrid's record 140-million-euro ($157 million) signing, scored his first goal for the club to help them shade Villarreal, but the game was marked by Vinicius's dismissal.
The Brazil international, on as a substitute, scored but his goal was disallowed and he was sent off after a VAR review showed he pulled the hair of Villarreal's Nathan Saliba in the build-up.
"Sorry to my team and the fans," said Vinicius on Instagram.
Mourinho's Madrid battled through the final stages with 10 men but held on to their slender lead earned by 19-year-old winger Diomande.
Despite Madrid's victory, Vinicius's red card left a bitter taste for Los Blancos, with the winger running the risk of a potential ban which could keep him out of the Clasico on October 25.
"I don't know what's going on with the referees, with this red card, I don't understand, but the most important thing is the victory," said Madrid midfielder Aurelien Tchouameni.
Mourinho declined to attend his post-match press conference in protest at the refereeing, a club source said.
The Madrid coach had complained bitterly about refereeing decisions which did not go his team's way in the derby defeat by Atletico before the recent international break.
Striker Kylian Mbappe was fit to start the match for Madrid and hit the post in a largely dull first half.
Home fans were not happy with the team at half-time but after 63 minutes they were able to celebrate Diomande's first goal, a sharp low finish into the far corner after being set up by Federico Valverde.
The drama with Vinicius followed, but in part thanks to goalkeeper Thibaut Courtois, Madrid were able to clinch three important points.
Earlier Cristian Romero's header in the 87th minute earned Atletico Madrid a narrow win at 10-man Alaves.
Alejandro Grimaldo put Atletico in front before Lucas Boye equalised from the penalty spot for Alaves before the interval.
Angel Perez was sent off for the hosts in the second half and Romero's header from Alex Baena's cross late on secured the victory.
"It's always important that the goal comes from wherever it comes, as long as it comes," said Simeone.

item.title: Ten-man Spurs rescue draw at Man Utd, Arsenal survive Leeds scare
item.description:
Ten-man Tottenham salvaged a 1-1 against fellow strugglers Manchester United thanks to Dominic Solanke's last-gasp leveller, while Arsenal got back on track as the champions survived a scare to beat Leeds 2-1 on Saturday.
In a clash dubbed 'El Sackicko' given the scrutiny on both managers, Bryan Mbeumo put United ahead in the 73rd minute at Old Trafford.
Mbeumo punished sloppy Tottenham marking to fire home from an acute angle after Matheus Cunha's pass picked him out in the penalty area.
Tottenham looked doomed when Uruguay midfielder Rodrigo Bentancur was sent off for headbutting United defender Luke Shaw in a brawl five minutes after United's opener.
But Solanke came to Tottenham's rescue in the final moments when he evaded United defender Lisandro Martinez to head in Sandro Tonali's cross.
It was a dramatic finale to a scrappy encounter in keeping with the problems gripping two underachieving teams.
Tottenham sit third bottom of the table and remain winless after losing three of their first six league games.
United are languishing in 12th place with only one league so far this season.
Roberto De Zerbi saved Tottenham from relegation on the final day of last term after taking charge late in the campaign.
But despite spending over £300 million ($429 million) on new signings in the close-season, Tottenham have failed to win any of their opening six games of a league season for just the fourth time in their history.
"I like the situation we were in with the red card. We need this situation. We have not accepted the defeat," De Zerbi said.
"I kiss Bentancur in the dressing room. Football is character. I'm very happy because I have seen the right spirit and character."
Carrick's side were hoping to build on last season's impressive third-place finish.
However, United's total of six points is their fewest at this stage of a campaign since 1986-87.
"For a number of reasons, we were not quite there. You could see it was a challenging time," Carrick said after United were booed off.
"It hurts a lot because I care about this club. But I understand the disappointment."
After a shock 3-0 defeat at Brighton before the international break, Arsenal were in danger of a second successive loss when they fell behind at the Emirates Stadium.
James Justin fired Leeds ahead in the 55th minute after Arsenal failed to clear Gabriel Gudmundsson's cross.
But Italy defender Riccardo Calafiori found the cure when he converted Ben White's header from close-range in the 62nd minute.
Arsenal showcased their strength in depth as substitute Bruno Guimaraes drilled the winner from the edge of the area just six minutes after coming on.
Guimaraes' first goal at the Emirates since his close-season move from Newcastle made it five wins from six league matches for the Gunners.
The north London club sit in second place behind crisis-hit Manchester City on goal difference.
City travel to Liverpool on Sunday for their first match since being found guilty of more than 100 breaches of Premier League financial rules.
"We weren't pleased against Brighton and today was an opportunity to put that right. We certainly reacted in the manner we expected," Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta said.
At Stamford Bridge, Chelsea's blistering start paved the way for a 5-1 rout of Bournemouth as the Blues won for the first time in four league matches.
Jordan Henderson gave Xabi Alonso's team the perfect start when the veteran midfielder curled home after just 68 seconds to claim his first goal for Chelsea.
The Blues struck again in the third minute through Morgan Rogers and Joao Pedro made it three soon after half-time.
Evanilson got one back for Bournemouth in the 51st minute as Chelsea's run without a league clean-sheet extended to 22 matches.
Joao Pedro put the result beyond doubt in the 67th minute and Henderson, 36, bagged his second in the 70th minute with a fierce free-kick.
Aston Villa's troubled start continued with a disappointing 2-2 home draw against Brentford.
Ipswich beat winless Fulham 2-1, while 10-man Brighton won 2-0 at Sunderland to cement their hold on third place.

item.title: Rahmat Shah leads Afghan fightback against Bangladesh
item.description:
Skipper Rahmat Shah showed a grit and impeccable determination to keep Bangladesh bowlers at bay as Afghanistan fought back to leave the one-off Test evenly poised on Day 2 at the Sheikh Jayed Stadium in Abu Dhabi, the United Arab Emirates (UAE) on Saturday.
Rahmat negotiated Bangladesh bowlers astutely throughout the day to remain not out on 84, steering Afghanistan to 211-4 at stumps. Ikram Ali Khil was on 26 after adding 72 runs with the skipper for an unbroken fifth wicket.
Afghanistan are still trailing by runs 135 runs.
Bangladesh were bowled out for 346 in its first innings, riding on half-centuries from openers Tanzid Hasan Tamim (83), Shadman Islam (67) and wicket-keeper batter Liton Das (53).
The platform of Afghan resurgence was set by opener Abdul Malik, who hit his maiden half-century before being out on 62.
Afghanistan began watchfully and kept Bangladesh waiting for 11 overs for the first wicket.
Hasan Mahmud, the hero of Darwin Test victory over Australia, gave the side the breakthrough, getting rid of Sediqullah Atal for 17.
The stubbornness of Malik made Bangladesh toiling before Ebadot struck with the wicket of Shahidullah who made 20.
However, Rahmat joined Malik to keep Bangladesh bowlers at bay, denying them making further inroads.
Bangladesh heaved a sigh of relief in the last session when they got two wickets in quick succession.
Ebadot struck again with a delivery that carried extra bounce and Malik edged behind, ending a 70-run partnership with Rahmat.
Two overs later, Mehidy Hasan Miraz had Hasmathullah Shahidi stumped for duck, leaving Afghanistan 139-4.
Bangladesh appeared to take the stranglehold from that stage. But Rahmat, with apt support from Ikram Alikhil defied Bangladesh attack to leave the side unscathed till the stumps.
Ebadot was the most successful bowler for Bangladesh with 2-50 while Hasan and Miraz picked up one wicket apiece.
Earlier, Bangladesh added 29 runs to their overnight total of 317-8, with overnight unbeaten batter Nayeem Hasan scoring most of the runs to remain unbeaten on 35.
Afghan pacer Mohammad Saleem claimed the wicket of Taijul Isalm for 9 to finish with team-best 4-82.
Yamin Ahmadzai dismissed Ebadot Hossain for duck, snapping up 3-79.

item.title: How to make aloo bhorta? What's your recipe?
item.description:
A hand shot up in the first row. The young university student gave his personal recipe for the spicy mashed potato concoction -- replete with mustard oil and fried dried chillies!

No, this was no cooking or catering class. This was a literary discussion on the debut novel, Appetite, by young author P Paromita. And the venue was Green University in the  beautiful Dhaka suburb of Purbachal. The institution's Department of English had organised the discussion for the faculty and students.

Kicking off the discussion, Associate Professor Dr Elham Hossain, lauded the author's use of food as a bridge to her Bangladeshi roots. Working as a chef in a restaurant in the US, the main character Zarina repeatedly would turn to desi ingredients to give a desi twist to her culinary creations. She exerted her Bangladeshi identity by repeatedly correcting persons who termed her as "Indian."

He also pointed out to the element of exploitation, a hangover of imperialism that lingered on -- her not being paid properly at her work place or for services rendered in promoting a star wrestler, the treatment meted out by a senior chef in the restaurant and so on.

He also pointed out how the author exposed the fickle world of fandom where fans were ready to almost give their lives for their idols, but were repaid with indifference and neglect. All these elements stripped away the illusions of civilisation in the western world.

Also speaking in the occasion was journalist Ayesha Kabir, head of Prothom Alo English Online. She said that P Paromita had opened up a new world for her through the book Appetite. As a new generation writer, P Paromita had presented the changed values of today's world, where the lines of class, gender, race and age were blurred. It is not that these discriminations didn't exist before, but the younger generation no longer viewed the world in the preconceived manner of their elders. A wrestler was a wrestler -- not a male wrestler or a female wrestler. The protagonist, ambitious young woman Zarina, had her eyes set on her goal of being a chef, not the stereotypical  "daktar-ingineer" as parents were wont to insist upon.

And food, aloo bhorta in particular, was a sort of metaphor, where chillies, onions and mustard oil, mashed up with boiled potatoes, seemed to describe Zarina's identity -- ambitions, desperations, dreams and angst that made her a whole and complete person. When she cooks shorshe ilish, it is not just an adaptation of Bangladeshi cuisine with western ingredients, it is her acceptance of both her roots and her adopted home in the US.

An appetite for aloo bhorta, shorshe salmon and wrestling

Joining the event were the Dean of the Faculty of Arts and Social Sciences, Dr M Shahidullah and the Chairman of the Department of English, Dr Md Shamim Mondol. They both appreciated that P Paramita was taking Bangladesh to the global literary sphere through her novel Appetite.

A lively interactive session with the students followed the presentations, where further details of the book and the author were discussed.

item.title: 2 Bangladeshis killed in Houthi missile attack at Riyadh airport, 4 in ICU
item.description:
Two Bangladeshis were killed in an attack by Houthi rebels at King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia. Four other Bangladeshis injured in the attack are receiving treatment in the intensive care unit (ICU) of King Khalid Hospital in Riyadh.

Foreign Affairs State Minister Shama Obaed Islam shared the information while responding to questions from journalists at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs on Sunday afternoon.

Earlier, when the Houthis launched an attack, a Bangladeshi was killed. Now, two more have been killed, the state minister said.

Referring to the 14 Bangladeshis who have already died in the Middle East conflict, Shama Obaed said, “We hope this disaster will end and these attacks will stop. It is extremely painful to accept such deaths.”

In a statement on Saturday’s attack in Riyadh, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs said a missile struck Terminal-3 of King Khalid International Airport at around 3:20pm on Saturday. Passengers from Bangladesh and several other countries were waiting at the terminal at the time.

Two Bangladeshi nationals were killed in the incident. They were Md Shahed Ahmed of Madla village in Shahjahanpur upazila of Bogura and Md Nasrullah Badarpuri of Badarpur village in Nangalkot upazila of Cumilla.

Diplomatic sources in Riyadh said Bangladeshi passengers travelling with US-Bangla Airlines, Saudia and Riyadh Air were at the airport during the attack.

Among the passengers who were not injured, 17 are staying at the Marriott Hotel, 25 at the Radisson Hotel and 40 at the residential hall of Princess Nourah University.

Four injured Bangladeshis are currently receiving treatment in the ICU of King Khalid Hospital. Two other passengers who were not injured are also staying there with them.

Shama Obaed said, “We are deeply saddened by this incident. We pray to Almighty Allah to grant them Jannah and we hope we will not receive any more bad news.”

The state minister also said the safety and welfare of Bangladeshis working abroad remained the government’s top priority.

“The prime minister always says that our first responsibility is to ensure the safety and look after the large number of Bangladeshis working abroad, our brothers and sisters who are our remittance warriors. That is our top priority and we are trying our best to fulfill it. Our mission there is keeping in touch with other Bangladeshis, gathering updates on the casualties, and taking necessary steps to ensure our people remain as safe as possible," she said.

Biman Bangladesh Airlines has temporarily suspended flights to Riyadh following the missile attack at the airport.

Asked whether any Bangladeshi flight was at King Khalid International Airport at the time of the attack or whether any Bangladeshi aircraft had been damaged, Shama Obaed said the government had no such information so far.

“We have no information of that kind so far. Flights were suspended as soon as we received news of the attack. We hope no such incident will happen again,” she said.

item.title: India’s ‘cockroach’ leaders vow to keep up election protests
item.description:
INDIA-POLITICS/GEN Z

Leaders of India’s online “cockroach” movement pledged on Sunday to continue their campaign against the election commissioner, hours after they were released from detention as authorities sought to thwart a major demonstration.

The rally planned for Saturday in the capital New Delhi came after weeks of opposition mobilisation following allegations of misconduct during a nationwide voter roll revision that critics say could benefit Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s ruling party.

The Election Commission of India, which oversees the voting process in the world’s most populous nation, has denied wrongdoing.

Abhijeet Dipke, founder of the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) protest movement, and two other leaders were detained on Saturday before they could disembark from their flight in Delhi ahead of the planned demonstration.

Thousands of protesters were also detained, according to the youth-led group and media reports.

“We will not back down,” CJP co-convenor Saurav Das said at a news conference in Delhi after his release from detention.

“We urge people to come out and carry out peaceful protests,” he added, vowing to continue until Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar resigns.

The protest leaders were released on the condition that they would maintain “peace for one year”, Ratna Singh, the CJP’s head lawyer, said in a social media post.

In July, protests organised by the CJP over exam irregularities forced the resignation of the education minister, marking a rare climbdown by Modi’s administration.

Ahead of Saturday’s rally, authorities mounted a sweeping security operation across the capital, shutting down metro stations and more than 200 trains while imposing a ban on public gatherings in several areas.

‘Important to show up’

The protest leaders were released on the condition that they would maintain “peace for one year”, Ratna Singh, the CJP’s head lawyer, said in a social media post.

The Supreme Court, hearing petitions challenging the detentions and other security measures, directed the authorities on Sunday to ensure protesters gathering peacefully are not detained illegally.

“Detention shall only be after following a legal procedure,” Justice Joymalya Bagchi said in oral remarks.

The court also ordered authorities to ensure there was no disruption to internet connectivity after mobile access was temporarily shut down around the Jantar Mantar protest site on Saturday.

Authorities have not commented on the detentions.

In a social media post soon after his release, Dipke took aim at Modi, who “as PM, is an embarrassment to India”, he said.

“Never has this country seen a bigger coward and bully.”

The youth movement has emerged as one of the most significant political challenges to Modi during his third term in power, winning millions of followers on social media since it was launched in May as a satirical party.

On Sunday, an AFP reporter saw dozens of people, including journalists, detained at three locations near Jantar Mantar, which remained fortified.

“I was detained for 10 hours yesterday,” said Aarti, 37, who gave only one name. “I have come again today because it is important to show up.”

‘Anger’

The revision of voter rolls at the centre of the protest campaign resulted in more than 133 million names being removed from electoral lists, according to media reports.

Critics say the revision has disproportionately affected minorities, particularly Muslims, potentially benefiting Modi’s Hindu nationalist Bharatiya Janata Party.

Election authorities say the revision was aimed at eliminating duplicate, deceased and fraudulent entries.

The detention of protesters on Saturday triggered sharp criticism and accusations that Modi’s government was stifling dissent.

The UN human rights office called for the immediate and unconditional release of all those “arbitrarily detained” in Delhi.

Rahul Gandhi of the opposition Congress party has also vowed to press ahead with protests against the election commission despite the crackdown.

Gandhi said his party “and the youth of the country will once again take to the streets in large numbers” on Monday.

“The more Modi and his government crack down, the more the anger of Gen Z and students will grow,” he said.

item.title: How MBA and EMBA degrees are becoming popular for boosting professional skills
item.description:
People are now leaning towards boosting their skills across local and global sectors. So the demand for Master of Business Administration (MBA) and Executive MBA (EMBA) degrees from the business faculties and institutes of various universities is growing steadily.

The Fourth Industrial Revolution, the rapid expansion of artificial intelligence and the rise of new business models have posed major challenges to traditional business operations. In today’s highly competitive job market, it is difficult to reach or maintain top-tier career positions relying solely on conventional experience or a standard undergraduate degree.

This is exactly why MBA and EMBA programs have gained immense popularity among professionals in Bangladesh. These programs offer them a golden opportunity to enhance their practical skills and prepare themselves to tackle complex, modern day business problems.

Opportunities for all

As business practices become more modernized, competition in both domestic and global markets is constantly rising. Consequently, the demand for highly skilled and forward thinking managers in the country’s leading corporate firms is growing every day.

EMBA classes typically start in the evening, allowing students to smoothly balance their academic pursuits with their jobs. This degree is highly valued by corporate professionals.

For most corporate professionals, quitting a job just to pursue an MBA does not make practical sense. The EMBA program has created a remarkable opportunity for working individuals, enabling them to upgrade their academic qualifications while maintaining their careers, thereby paving the way for continuous professional growth.

There was a time when a general MBA program was the primary key to securing promotions in the corporate world, focusing largely on overall business management and fundamental business strategies. However, the corporate world has now become far more complex. General management knowledge alone is no longer enough to navigate complex corporate crises. There is a distinct need for deep, specialized expertise as well.

EMBA courses equip students with the strategic knowledge and versatile skills required to tackle multidimensional problems and thrive in today’s cutting edge, competitive and dynamic business environments, both locally and globally.

To establish oneself as a business leader and secure top tier roles in domestic or multinational companies, there is simply no alternative to an EMBA program.

Keeping pace with the times, EMBA programs now feature essential subjects like artificial intelligence, business analytics, agri-business management, fintech, machine learning, deep learning and quantitative business analysis, all taught by experienced faculties.

Aside classroom-based learning, these programs ensure that the students gain exceptional practical knowledge and skills through corporate exchange sessions, real time case studies, guest lectures, corporate visits, simulations, industry-led projects and seminars. These programmes also provide opportunities for participants to build professional networks with corporate employees from different sectors.

Classroom mirrors corporate meeting room

Classroom based learning helps students develop data driven decision making skills, which are increasingly important in modern corporate environments.

Alongside fundamental concepts in financial analysis, strategic marketing, supply chain management and human resource development, students learn how to analyse real-world data to identify and mitigate business risks.

By working on international case studies, students gain insights into economic risks in emerging markets and learn practical approaches to managing company resources amid uncertainty.

Group discussions and presentations also help develop strategic leadership and negotiation skills. Through classroom simulations, they get hands-on experience in managing multidisciplinary teams and executing strategic ‘pivots’ during crises to keep businesses profitable.

The programmes also help students understand business ethics and corporate governance while developing the ability to adapt to technological changes.

Professionals with MBA degrees can apply their knowledge to make effective and informed business decisions, contributing to organisational growth and improved performance. Greater efficiency can help businesses strengthen their positions in both domestic and international markets.

Participation in MBA and EMBA programmes can also strengthen professionals' analytical and critical thinking abilities, helping them make better informed business decisions. Many continue to pursue new knowledge and update their skills even after completing their degrees. This habit of continuous learning can help them respond more effectively to unfamiliar and complex business challenges.

Opportunities in Bangladesh

Globally renowned institutions such as Harvard, INSEAD and the Indian Institutes of Management (IIMs) offer specialised EMBA programmes alongside their conventional degrees.

Universities in Bangladesh are also revising their curricula and introducing MBA and EMBA programmes to meet international industry demands.

Professionals can apply to these programmes by sitting for admission tests, which are generally held in two or three sessions a year. Weekend and hybrid learning models are also providing working professionals with greater flexibility in scheduling their studies.

Admission tests typically include multiple-choice and written questions covering English, mathematics, analytical reasoning, current affairs and general knowledge.

Applicants with an undergraduate degree from a recognised university in Bangladesh and an acceptable academic record may qualify for admission. Completing an EMBA programme generally takes at least two years.

However, admission schedules, examination formats, curricula and eligibility requirements vary from one university to another.

item.title: Eight writers receive BRAC Bank–Samakal Literary Award
item.description:
Eight prominent poets, fiction writers, researchers and literary figures received the BRAC Bank–Samakal Literary Awards and honours for 2024 and 2025 at a ceremony in Dhaka on Friday evening.

The awards for the two years were presented at the Grand Ballroom of Pan Pacific Sonargaon Hotel. Emeritus Professor Serajul Islam Choudhury received the Lifetime Achievement Award for 2024, while fiction writer Selina Hossain received the honour for 2025.

Nizam Biswas won the 2024 Young Writer Award for his book Jolmakorer Noukabaich, published by Baitarani Prokashon. Professor Abul Ahsan Choudhury won in the essay, autobiography and translation category for his collection Vidyasagar, Bankimchandra, Rabindranath and Musolman Samaj, published by Anyaprokash. Anwara Syed Haq received the award in the poetry and fiction category for her novel Shomoy Bohiya Gelo, published by Prothoma Prokashon.

For 2025, Mahbub Mayukh Rishad won the Young Writer Award for his novel Cyanide Phool, published by Anyaprokash. His wife received the award on his behalf.

Nasreen Jahan won in the essay, autobiography and translation category for Paloker Chinhogulo (Autobiographical Memoir), published by Bengal Books. Shaheen Akhtar received the award in the poetry and fiction category for Manchitra, published by Batighar.

Despite being physically unwell, Nasreen Jahan attended the ceremony. In a brief speech after receiving her award, she spoke about her illness, thoughts of death and determination to live.

“I learned on the afternoon of last year's Samakal Literary Award ceremony that I had cancer. I have spent this past year thinking about death. Doctors say I need surgery to remove my gallbladder and transplants for both kidneys. I had more or less accepted death. I thought perhaps I would not be able to come here next year. But suddenly it occurred to me: does death ask us anything? We cannot hear it, but we agree and then leave. I am not agreeing. Let's see what happens,” she said.

Video clips featuring brief profiles of the award-winning writers, their professional and personal lives, and their reactions to receiving the honours were shown on a large screen during the ceremony.

Speaking as chief guest, economist Wahiduddin Mahmud said freedom of thought must be ensured in literature and creative pursuits. He stressed the importance of private initiatives alongside government support for literary activities, adding that such patronage must remain above narrow partisan interests.

Highlighting the contributions of Lifetime Achievement Award recipient Serajul Islam Choudhury, Wahiduddin Mahmud said the professor had remained steadfast in his principles throughout his life in opposing injustice and oppression. Through his writings on contemporary society and politics, he had also raised awareness across generations.

His work spans essays, research, translation and children's literature, Wahiduddin Mahmud said, adding that figures such as Choudhury had made lifelong contributions to building a knowledge-oriented and culturally conscious society.

Times Media Limited Managing Director and Samakal publisher AK Azad congratulated the award recipients. He said the development of society and culture could not depend solely on the government and that private institutions, including banks, should also contribute to social and cultural initiatives.

Many talented people across the country remain unnoticed because they lack opportunities, he said. With encouragement and recognition, they could produce work of greater value.

BRAC Bank Vice-Chairperson Faruq Mayeenuddin Ahmed said many literary awards had once been launched through private initiatives, but most had failed to survive. Sustaining such initiatives required long-term commitment and a clear vision, he said.


“An award does not make literature greater, but recognising the work of writers is a responsibility of society and the corporate sector,” he said, expressing hope that the BRAC Bank–Samakal Literary Award would never be discontinued.

Faizul Latif Chowdhury, a member of the jury, outlined the selection process, saying a total of 36 books had been evaluated for the awards covering the two years. The evaluation criteria varied according to the type of book.

He emphasised the important role publishers play in submitting quality books for consideration and noted that relatively few poetry collections had been entered.

Samakal Editor Shahed Mohammad Ali, who chaired the ceremony, thanked the award-winning writers, invited guests and BRAC Bank for remaining associated with the initiative for 15 years. He also congratulated the publishers of the winning books.

Prominent figures from the country's arts, literature, culture and politics attended the ceremony.

item.title: Sajek road blockade begins indefinitely, leaving tourists stranded
item.description:
An indefinite road blockade called by two organisations began in Sajek, in Rangamati’s Baghaichhari upazila, at 6:00 am on Sunday. The blockade has halted traffic on the main road leading to the Ruilui tourist destination in Sajek.

Since morning, protesters have been seen demonstrating at various points along the road, placing tree trunks across it and setting tyres on fire in support of the blockade. They have also been preventing vehicles from passing.

The two organisations behind the blockade are the Sajek Karbari Association and the Sajek Gana Adhikar Committee (people’s rights protection committee).

Speaking about the situation, Tuntu Moni Chakma, president of the Khagrachhari Mahindra Owners Welfare Cooperative Association, told Prothom Alo, “This is the peak tourist season. On average, around 2,500 tourists travel to Sajek every day in about 30 Mahindra vehicles and jeeps. Many tourists also set off from Khagrachhari town for Sajek this morning. Because of the blockade, they could not travel beyond Baghaihat. However, they are expected to be taken to Sajek under the escort of security forces at around 2:00 pm.”

Rahul Chakma, organising secretary of the Sajek Resort-Cottage Owners Association, told Prothom Alo that some tourists had left Sajek the previous day after hearing about the blockade, while others had arrived.

“Altogether, around 3,000 tourists are currently staying in Sajek,” he said.

He added that no vehicles carrying tourists had left Sajek for Khagrachhari in the morning. Tourist vehicles were expected to depart at 2:00 pm.

Babudhan Chakma, convener of the Sajek Gana Adhikar Committee, told Prothom Alo that their previously announced road blockade had been proceeding peacefully since 6:00 am.

Alleging that protesters had faced obstruction while picketing at various locations, he said, “The blockade would continue until our demands were met.”

Asked about the situation, Sajek police station officer-in-charge Toffazzal Hossain told Prothom Alo that no vehicles were operating in Sajek. All tourist vehicles would leave Sajek under the escort of security forces at 2:00 pm, while vehicles from Baghaihat would head towards Sajek at the same time.

Why the blockade?

The Sajek Karbari Association and the Sajek Gana Adhikar Committee have alleged that the regional political organisation JSS (Jana Samhati Samiti), led by Santu Larma, has begun armed activities in Sajek and is threatening and intimidating local residents.

The two organisations held a rally last Thursday and set a deadline for action against those responsible. They called the road blockade after, they said, no action was taken within the stipulated time.

JSS, however, has dismissed the allegations that it is threatening and intimidating local residents, describing them as baseless. It claims the two organisations announced the blockade under pressure from the United People’s Democratic Front (UPDF).

Sajib Chakma, publicity secretary of JSS, told Prothom Alo, “These allegations are being raised to divert attention from the long-standing oppression and harassment of innocent people in Sajek by armed UPDF members.”

Asked for comment, UPDF spokesperson Angya Marma told Prothom Alo that no organisation had called the blockade under pressure from the UPDF.

However, he said the UPDF would support the programme announced by the two organisations on behalf of local residents.

item.title: TOP SHOTS (11 October 2026)
Bangladesh dominate second session to take 230-run lead against Afghanistan
item.description:
Bangladesh strengthened their position against Afghanistan on the third day of the one-off Test, reaching 124 for three in their second innings at the end of the second session to build a lead of 230 runs.

Mushfiqur Rahim was batting on 48 and Najmul Hossain Shanto on 23 at the break, with the pair adding an unbeaten 71-run partnership after Bangladesh lost three wickets for 53 runs.

Opener Tanzid Hasan was the only Bangladesh batter dismissed in the second session, scoring 31 off 38 balls. He was caught at second slip off Yamin Ahmadzai after edging a back-of-a-length delivery.

Najmul and Mushfiq then steadied the innings, helping Bangladesh recover from the early setbacks. Najmul also survived an lbw appeal after successfully reviewing the umpire’s decision, with replays showing the ball would have missed the stumps.

Bangladesh had resumed the third day with a 104-run lead after scoring 346 in their first innings. Afghanistan, who had started the day at 211 for four, were bowled out for 240, adding just 29 runs while losing their remaining six wickets.

Hasan Mahmud took four of those six wickets to finish with five for 55, while Ebadot Hossain claimed the other two to end with four for 56. Hasan also became the first Bangladesh fast bowler to take a hat-trick.

Afghanistan captain Rahmat Shah scored an unbeaten 105, his fourth Test century and second against Bangladesh. Azmatullah Omarzai contributed 62.

Brief scores

Bangladesh, first innings: 346 (Tanzid Hasan 83, Sadman Islam 67; Mohammad Saleem 4/82, Yamin Ahmadzai 3/79).

Afghanistan, first innings: 240 (Rahmat Shah 105 not out, Azmatullah Omarzai 62; Hasan Mahmud 5/55, Ebadot Hossain 4/56).

Bangladesh, second innings: 124/3 in 36 overs (Mushfiqur Rahim 48 not out, Najmul Hossain Shanto 23 not out).
Bangladesh lead by 230 runs.

item.title: INGO Forum on Eye Health and NIOH jointly observe World Sight Day
item.description:
State Minister for Health & Family Welfare, MA Muhit, MP, calls for stronger Government–NGO Collaboration to protect vision through greater awareness and affordable eye care services, reports a press release.

The INGO Forum on Eye Health in Bangladesh, in collaboration with the National Institute of Ophthalmology & Hospital (NIOH), recently commemorated World Sight Day 2026 under the global theme, “Love Your Eyes”, bringing together government leaders, eye health professionals, development partners, and civil society representatives to reaffirm their commitment to ensuring equitable access to quality eye care services for all people in Bangladesh.

The programme, held at the Durga P Paudyal Conference Hall, CIRDAP, Dhaka, began with a rally inaugurated by MA Muhit, MP, State Minister for Health & Family Welfare, followed by a discussion session focused on eye health, accessibility, and the broader social and economic value of eye care.

Addressing the audience as Chief Guest, MA Muhit, MP said, “Vision is fundamental to learning, work, safe mobility, and active participation in society. World Sight Day reminds us that many forms of visual impairment and blindness can be prevented or effectively addressed through timely eye care. By strengthening awareness and expanding affordable, accessible eye care services through enhanced collaboration among government institutions, private healthcare providers, and development partners, we can help millions of people protect and improve their sight.”

The discussion was opened by Amrita Rejina Rozario, chair of the INGO Forum on Eye Health in Bangladesh and Country Director of Sightsavers Bangladesh. Highlighting the burden of visual impairment in the country, she said: “According to the Nationwide Blindness Survey 2020, 19 per cent of people aged 30 and over experience some form of visual impairment. The impact extends far beyond vision loss. For children, it can affect education and social development, while for adults it often limits independence, mobility, productivity, and economic opportunities. On behalf of the INGO Forum on Eye Health, I urge greater public investment and stronger GO-NGO collaboration to ensure that quality eye care reaches everyone, particularly those in underserved and hard-to-reach communities.”

Delivering the keynote presentation on behalf of the INGO Forum on Eye Health, Misha Mahjabeen, managing director of VisionSpring Bangladesh, emphasised the transformative impact of access to eyeglasses and vision services.

She stated, “A pair of eyeglasses may seem simple, but the impact can be life-changing. Clear vision improves learning, livelihoods, safety, and independence. Our commitment is to bring vision screening and affordable glasses closer to communities facing barriers. World Sight Day offers stakeholders a chance to unite and boost efforts for a future where everyone who needs glasses can get them.”

Md Mohsin, joint secretary of the Health Services Division, ministry of Health and Family Welfare, attended the programme as special guest and shared his remarks on the importance of integrating eye health into broader health system strengthening efforts.

The session was chaired by Syeed Mehbub Ul Kadir, director of the National Institute of Ophthalmology & Hospital (NIOH), who highlighted the importance of coordinated efforts to advance eye health services across Bangladesh.

Among other Special Guests were Munir Ahmed, country chair of the Bangladesh Chapter of the International Agency for the Prevention of Blindness (IAPB) and Country Director of Orbis International; Prof Md Zinnu Rain (Newton), secretary general of the Ophthalmological Society of Bangladesh (OSB); and Md Tauhidur Rahman, president of OSB, who also shared their remarks. The discussion was moderated by Afsana Habib Sheuly, programme head at Helen Keller Intl.

World Sight Day, observed annually on the second Thursday of October, raises global awareness about eye health.

Led by the International Agency for the Prevention of Blindness (IAPB), it encourages governments, organisations, and individuals to prioritise accessible, quality eye care. In 2026, World Sight Day was observed on 8 October.

The programme concluded with a vote of thanks delivered on behalf of the Co-Chair of the INGO Forum on Eye Health, AKM Badrul Huq, senior programme manager at The Fred Hollows Foundation. He reaffirmed the Forum’s commitment to working alongside the government and partners to achieve universal access to eye health services in Bangladesh.

item.title: Sobhana Mostary hits century against Australia in Brisbane
item.description:
Sobhana Mostary could barely keep out an Annabel Sutherland delivery. As soon as she did, Nigar Sultana, at the non-striker’s end, set off for a run, and Sobhana ran with her.

Even after reaching the popping crease, Sobhana continued running well beyond it. After all, it was a century!

And it was no ordinary opposition she was facing. Australia are a powerhouse in women’s cricket. Sobhana celebrated by raising her bat and embracing Nigar at the other end, while her teammates’ excitement was clearly visible in the dressing room.

Sobhana scored a century against Australia in Brisbane today in the second match of the three-match series. She became the first Bangladesh women’s cricketer to score a century against Australia.

In the six previous ODIs Bangladesh’s women had played against Australia, both at home and away, they had never reached 200 runs. Today, Bangladesh batted through their full 50 overs to post 220 for six.

Bangladesh had scored 153 in the first ODI of the series. Against Australia’s pace attack and on a bouncy pitch, that was not a particularly poor total. Today, however, Bangladesh got off to another disastrous start with the bat. By 7.2 overs, they had lost three wickets for just eight runs.

Sobhana Mostary and Nigar Sultana then steadied the innings. The pair gradually rebuilt Bangladesh’s innings through a partnership. Sobhana reached her half-century off 66 balls, while captain Nigar provided excellent support, remaining unbeaten on 74 off 114 balls.

Their partnership took Bangladesh past the 100-run mark. Sobhana then brought up her century off 124 balls. She became the eighth batter to score a century against Australia on Australian soil. She is also the third Bangladesh batter to score an ODI century, after Fargana Haque, who has two centuries, and Nigar Sultana, who has one.

Sobhana was eventually bowled by Megan Schutt for 118 off 134 balls, an innings featuring 18 fours. Her 243-ball partnership with Nigar produced 195 runs.

item.title: Spend every penny of public money in national interest, PM orders officials
item.description:
Prime Minister Tarique Rahman on Sunday directed government officials to ensure that every penny allocated for development projects is spent properly in the interests of the country and its people.
“Many projects have been undertaken and many targets set. The government will allocate budgets to achieve those targets. But this is public money. I hope you will all pay attention to ensuring that every penny is spent properly in the national interest and for the welfare of people,” he said.
The prime minister made the remarks at a meeting to review the activities of the Ministry of Fisheries and Livestock and the progress of its various development projects at the ministry’s conference room at Secretariat.
Officials briefed him on the ministry’s ongoing activities, development projects, future plans and targets.
Urging officials to view public service as an opportunity to work for people, Tarique said those holding government positions were privileged compared with the country’s overall population.
“We are all privileged compared with the overall population of Bangladesh. Almighty Allah has given us an opportunity to work for our country and its people,” he said.
Tarique urged officials to perform their duties sincerely, according to their respective responsibilities and capabilities.
The prime minister said opportunities to serve in public office did not last forever, and everyone should make proper use of the time available to them to work for the welfare of the country and its people.
“Let us all try to make proper use of the opportunity, for as long as we have it, to work for people and the country,” he said at the end of the meeting.
Tarique Rahman also encouraged officials to share their views more actively, saying their field-level experience and observations could play an important role in government decision-making.
He said the progress of the ministry’s activities would be reviewed again in future meetings, expressing hope that officials would speak more openly about their experiences, observations and opinions.
Fisheries and Livestock Minister Mohammad Amin Ur Rashid, State Minister Sultan Salauddin Tuku and senior ministry officials attended the meeting.
